[[Jimmy Kennedy (hurler born 1926)|Jimmy Kennedy]] (4–8) | previous = [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship 1947|1947]] | next = [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship 1949|1949]] }} The '''1948 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship''' was the 62nd staging of the All-Ireland [[hurling]] championship since its establishment by the [[Gaelic Athletic Association]] in 1887. The championship began on 16 May 1948 and ended on 5 September 1948. [[Kilkenny GAA|Kilkenny]] entered the championship as the [[1947 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|defending champions]], however, they were beaten by [[Laois GAA|Laois]] in the [[#Leinster semi-finals|Leinster semi-finals]]. The [[1948 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship final|All-Ireland final]] was played on 5 September 1948 at [[Croke Park]] in [[Dublin]], between [[Waterford GAA|Waterford]] and [[Dublin GAA|Dublin]], in what was their second meeting in the final overall and a first meeting in the final in [[1938 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship final|10 years]]. Waterford won the match by 6–07 to 4–02 to claim their first ever All-Ireland title ==Format== The All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship was run on a provincial basis as usual. All games were played on a knockout basis whereby once a team lost they were eliminated from the championship. The format for the All-Ireland series of games ran as follows: * The winners of the [[Leinster Senior Hurling Championship|Leinster Championship]] advanced directly to the first All-Ireland semi-final. * The winners of the [[Munster Senior Hurling Championship|Munster Championship]] advanced directly to the second All-Ireland semi-final. * [[Antrim GAA|Antrim]], the representatives from the [[Ulster Senior Hurling Championship|Ulster Championship]], were drawn to play the Leinster champions in the All-Ireland semi-final. * [[Galway GAA|Galway]], a team who faced no competition in the [[Connacht Senior Hurling Championship|Connacht Championship]], entered the championship at the All-Ireland semi-final stage where they were drawn to play the Munster champions. ==Provincial
